clue.text: Something of a spectacle

parts.note: one who makes a spectacle of themselves is a laughing stock, the thing everyone stares at; the plain sense is simply any thing at all

explanation.surface: A bit of a show, or perhaps a glimpse of someone's eyeglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacle' tempts towards glasses, but the clue means a sight people gape at, as in making a fool of oneself; the answer is also the plainest word for 'something'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing gazed upon, or a sorry sight, is called this, and the word is also a general term for any item.

clue.text: Parrot subscribed to departure from gold standard

indicators.note: subscribed means written underneath, so in a down clue the parrot comes after
a departure from the word gold rearranges its letters

parts.note: a lory is a kind of brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A parrot signing up to abandon the gold standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold standard' is a false phrase: 'standard' alone is the definition, a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname of the United States flag, and a flag is a standard.

clue.text: Kitty gives John a drug

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of John
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A man named John handing over drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money staked in a game, as is a jackpot, the accumulated prize.

clue.text: Temperate part of the world

explanation.surface: A region of the globe with a mild climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained or abstemious, and also one of the earth's great landmasses such as Asia.

clue.text: A novel lot of health workers, five hundred and one

parts.note: WHO is the World Health Organization, a body of health workers
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: Counting a group of medical staff, apparently five hundred and one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A novel' is the definition, not an anagram signal: a detective story is a kind of novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective mystery is a type of book or fiction, so a novel can be one.

clue.text: Get London house repaired and keep quiet about it

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Get your London home fixed up and don't tell anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to refrain from speaking, staying silent on a matter.

clue.text: What is worn by a female physician?

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
-ess is a suffix marking a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A question about what a woman doctor wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about clothing, but the second part builds a jokey female doctor, DR + ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock or gown is clothing that is put on and worn.

clue.text: Piece of music heard in church service here

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a nocturne is a dreamy piece of night music

explanation.surface: A piece of music listened to during worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points to this answer: the nocturn is the service itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of matins, the night office of prayer.

clue.text: A farmer is used to steer

explanation.surface: A farmer employed to steer something.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tills the soil is a cultivator, and the bar on a boat's rudder steers it.

clue.text: Man somewhere in New Zealand -or in Durham

parts.note: a bishop is a chess man
Auckland is the largest city in New Zealand

explanation.surface: A man located either in New Zealand or in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere' serves the definition too: a place in County Durham, north-east England. 'Man' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishop Auckland is a market town in County Durham, seat of the Bishops of Durham.

clue.text: Variety of celandine coming up every few years

indicators.note: a variety of the word is a different version, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of wild flower that blooms only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decennial recurs once each ten years, which is a gap of a few years.

clue.text: Out of a hundred, the Spanish do best

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Scoring top marks in a Spanish exam, out of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo others or perform supremely well is to shine; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Scandinavian drink? Pshaw?!

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
pish and pshaw are both exclamations of contempt

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully dismissing a Nordic beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lapps are the Sami people of northern Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lappish describes the Sami people of the far north of Norway, Sweden and Finland, so it is a northern European adjective.

clue.text: Humble degree Open University confines to engineers

indicators.note: the university's letters enclose the degree, holding it inside

parts.note: BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A modest qualification from a distance-learning university restricted to engineering students.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of humble birth comes from lowly, unknown origins, which is this adjective's sense.

clue.text: Get pensioned off, losing the right to join up again

indicators.note: losing means the letter for right is dropped from the word

parts.note: to retire is to leave work on a pension
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pensioner gives up the right to re-enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up again' looks like re-enlisting, but it means knotting together a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten a knot or bow once more is to bind together a second time.

clue.text: Bird hard: for countryman to ensnare

indicators.note: the countryman traps the letter for hard inside himself

parts.note: a peasant is a rural labourer
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A game bird that is difficult for a rural man to trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-tailed game fowl shot for sport is one example of a bird.

clue.text: By mistake, re-engages Hugh to speak

indicators.note: letters arranged by mistake are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Hugh mistakenly hires someone back and has to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugh to speak' is Hugh said out loud, a hue: a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a soft greyish green, a colour or shade.

clue.text: Many a sailor follows it

parts.note: loads means many or lots
tar is a familiar word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Lots of seamen steer by a guiding star.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is the guiding star, Polaris, that navigators steer by.

clue.text: Beware of little drops of water starting corrosion

parts.note: mist is fine droplets of water in the air
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A warning that damp leads to rust.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wary of or doubt something is to have no faith in it.

clue.text: Take a drink, eluding getting drunk

indicators.note: the word becomes drunk, staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Having a drink, dodging getting tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge is to treat oneself, especially to alcohol.

clue.text: Enjoyment got us into trouble

indicators.note: putting the words into trouble disorders their letters

explanation.surface: Having fun landed us in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest, a keen pleasure.

clue.text: A foreigner, I'm in the prosperous part of the country finding quarters.

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the south-east

parts.words: the prosperous part of the country
parts.note: SE is the south-east of England, the wealthiest region
I'm expands to I am
S and E are two compass quarters

explanation.surface: A foreigner says he is in the wealthy south looking for lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings but means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese person is from Siam, now Thailand, so is an alien to Britons.

clue.text: Breathe hard, that's a good idea

explanation.surface: Someone puffing while announcing a brilliant plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheeze is to breathe with a whistling rasp, and a wheeze is also a clever scheme or trick.

clue.text: Swimmer owned a pool

parts.note: had means owned or possessed
a dock is an enclosed basin of water for ships

explanation.surface: Someone who once had their own swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer in crosswords can be a fish, and this is a North Atlantic food fish.

clue.text: With others, put into rising group

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the assembly is reversed
put means the abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: into can mean to, as in going towards
etc, et cetera, means and others

explanation.surface: Others are added to a group that is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: ETC goes inside TO to make TETCO; 'rising' reverses it, reading up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight players or singers, a musical ensemble.

clue.text: Horse in draw rejected as a screw

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in means the horse sits inside the word for draw

parts.note: to drain is to draw off liquid
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse in a tied race being turned away as a broken-down nag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is slang for a miser, someone tight with money. The horse GG goes inside DRAIN to give DRAGGIN, which 'rejected' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is slang for a stingy person, and a niggard is a miser.

clue.text: Distinction enjoyed by smart Alec latterly.

indicators.note: the letters are held and possessed within the phrase, as something enjoyed is owned

explanation.surface: A know-all who has lately found fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant success or acclaim, a mark of renown.

clue.text: A maiden was not accustomed to embrace me for fun

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the word for was not accustomed wraps around the second word, holding it inside

parts.note: usen't is an old contraction of used not
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman unused to being hugged, perhaps just for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: USEN'T is an old-fashioned form of 'used not'; ME goes inside it to give USEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment or merriment, a synonym for fun.

clue.text: Incident thought to be without a time

parts.note: an event is an incident or occurrence

indicators.note: without means the letter is removed from the word for thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: An occurrence considered timeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, a part of the day.

clue.text: Make valuable, point, attracting attention

parts.note: the end is the point or tip
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Advice to make a worthwhile point that will get people listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone dear to another is to make them beloved or precious.
